sections.title: Imports for audit logging

sections.name: AuditAction
sections.title: Categories of audited actions
sections.what: A fixed list of event labels for viewing, creating, changing, deleting, and exporting health information, plus logins and granting or removing access.
sections.why: Gives each audit row a fixed label so that reports can filter by event type.
sections.watch_out: The record function also accepts free text, so a misspelled action is saved without any error.

sections.name: AuditService
sections.title: Writing audit records safely
sections.what: Builds the audit row from the request and the given details, saves it, logs critical events, and logs a failed save without stopping the request.
sections.why: The header states that it tracks who accessed what, when, and from where.
sections.watch_out: A failed save is only logged, so the audit trail can have silent gaps.

summary: Writes a permanent record of who did what to health information, when, and from which device or address.
purpose: Creates the audit trail that health and privacy rules such as HIPAA and India's DPDP expect.
why: The header names HIPAA and DPDP compliance, so the purpose is stated.
how: 1) A feature passes in the user, the action, the resource, and optionally the request. 2) The service reads the IP address and browser details from the request. 3) It saves an audit row. 4) If the severity is critical, it writes an error log line. 5) If saving fails, it logs the failure and returns without stopping the request.
inputs: User id, action type, resource name, resource id, old and new data, severity, and the request.
outputs: A saved audit log row, or nothing if the save failed.
risks: A failed save is only logged, so an audit gap can go unnoticed. A critical event only writes a log line. The code comment mentions an alert to a security channel, but that alert is not implemented. The IP address can come from a forwarded header that a client may fake unless a trusted proxy sets it.
debug: If audit rows are missing, search the logs for the failure message from this file and check the audit table and the database client. If critical events raise no alert, confirm whether an alert integration exists elsewhere.
